$comment: Where each kind of source file is required to be covered, per Article V's three-layer separation.
The default pre-commit gate asks whether a source file has a co-located test of
the same name. That is the right question for pure logic and the wrong question
for a React Server Component or a Server Action: a `page.test.tsx` that reaches
PostgreSQL is neither 100% mocked nor under 10ms, so it would not be a unit test
under Article V — writing one to satisfy a filename check produces test theatre
and dilutes a suite that currently catches real defects.
This policy keeps the gate strict where mocked unit tests genuinely belong, and
redirects it to the correct layer everywhere else. Coverage is still mandatory;

requireColocatedTest.$comment: Pure logic. Cheap to test in isolation, and where the highest-value assertions live. A new file here must ship with <leaf>.test.ts.

coveredByLayer.reason: Routes, Server Actions and RSC pages are exercised end to end with real browser events (Article V, UX layer).
Interactive components are exercised through the journeys that use them, with cypress-real-events.
Schema, policies and RPCs are exercised against real PostgreSQL via testcontainers — never a mocked driver.

notSourceLogic.$comment: Declarations, configuration, operational tooling and the test suites themselves. Nothing here carries product logic that a unit test could meaningfully assert.
